title: Discovered attacks
summary: Move one piece out of the way and unleash the one behind it. When the hidden piece gives check, it is a discovered check.

steps.title: The hidden attacker
steps.text: White's bishop on b2 aims at the rook on h8, but its own knight on d4 is in the way. When the knight jumps, the bishop's attack is uncovered. That is a discovered attack: two threats from one move. Here the knight jumps with check, so Black must save the king, and the bishop takes the rook.
steps.narration: See the bishop on b2? It wants the rook on h8, but your own knight is blocking it. So the knight jumps to c6, with check! [move] Black has to save the king. [move] And the bishop's hidden attack takes the rook. [move]

steps.title: Discovered check
steps.prompt: Move the bishop off the e-file with check, and attack the queen at the same time.
steps.hint: Once the bishop moves, the rook on e1 checks the king. Which bishop square also hits a4?
steps.success: Bc2+ uncovers the rook's check on the e-file, and the bishop now eyes the queen through b3. Black must answer the check, so Bxa4 wins the queen.
steps.narration: Your bishop is standing between your rook and Black's king. Any bishop move is check from the rook, so make it count: find the square where the bishop also attacks the queen on a4.

steps.title: Take with check
steps.prompt: Your rook and Black's queen face each other on the e-file. Win the queen.
steps.hint: The bishop blocks the e-file. Move it with check, grabbing a pawn on the way.
steps.success: Bxh7+ is check from the bishop and uncovers the rook on the queen. Black has to deal with the check, and Rxe8+ takes the queen.
steps.narration: Right now your bishop blocks your own rook from Black's queen. Take the pawn on h7 with check. Black is busy with the king, and the rook takes the queen.

steps.title: Why it works
steps.question: Why are discovered checks so strong?

options.text: The piece that moves can go almost anywhere and grab something, because the opponent must answer the check first
options.why: The check comes from the piece behind, so the moving piece is free to attack, capture or even hang itself. The opponent only has time for the king.

options.text: A discovered check can never be blocked
options.why: It can be blocked like any check from a rook, bishop or queen. Its strength is that the other piece makes a second threat at the same time.

options.text: The moving piece cannot be captured
options.why: It can be captured, just not while the king is in check. That is why it gets away with so much.

steps.narration: Last one. What makes a discovered check so dangerous? Think about which piece gives the check, and what the other piece gets to do meanwhile. Nicely done today!
